items.ja: トマトたっぷりバターチキンカレー
items.note: A tomato curry finished with butter and cream, with yoghurt-marinated chicken, served over Tenri-grown rice mixed with black rice, plus a tofu-and-salted-kelp salad. Ask whether the curry is thickened with flour.

items.ja: とろけるチーズチキンカレー
items.note: The same curry base under a blanket of melted cheese; comes with salad. The two curries are the whole curry menu.

items.ja: 天然酵母のハーフサイズピザ
items.romaji: tennen kobo no haafu saizu piza
items.note: Small naturally-leavened pizza — wheat dough. Often shaped and decorated as a cat's face (ねこピザ neko-piza), which is what most of the photos on this shop are of.

items.ja: サンドイッチとドリンクのセット
items.note: Wheat-bread sandwich with a drink.

items.en: Cake of the day with a drink
items.note: Whatever is baked that day plus a drink; around ¥880 if you upgrade the drink. Cakes seen include New York cheesecake, white-chocolate cheesecake, caramel-banana cheesecake and chiffon cake.

items.ja: ニューヨークチーズケーキ
items.note: Dense baked cheesecake on a biscuit base; served with cream and ice cream on a deer-patterned plate.
Price quoted is with a coffee. Airy wheat-flour sponge.
Soft-set egg-and-milk custard with caramel — normally wheat-free by recipe, but this kitchen bakes cakes, so ask.
Rotating parfaits — grape, caramel-orange, banana, black-bean-and-kinako, and a striped 'tora-neko' (tabby cat) one. Usually layered with cornflakes or sponge, so treat as wheat.

items.ja: きんかんとほうじ茶のマフィン
items.note: Sold from the shopfront counter alongside other take-away sweets; hojicha is roasted green tea.
The shop's name means 'four leaves'; a small clover-shaped cookie comes free with drinks.
Price from a 2015 report. Comes with the clover cookie (which is wheat).

items.ja: 自家製レモネードソーダ
items.note: Made in-house.
Served as two visible layers you stir together yourself.
Kansai-style blended banana-and-fruit shake; contains milk.

items.en: Omurice — ketchup-seasoned chicken rice under a soft omelette
items.note: The shop names this and its home-made cakes as its two specialities. The 'torotoro tamago' style means the egg is left barely set and cut open at the table.

items.ja: オムピラフオンカレー
items.note: House speciality — pilaf, omelette and curry sauce in one plate; sold in 'dai' (large) size too. Japanese curry sauce is a wheat-flour roux.

items.ja: ピラフ きのこクリームソース
items.note: A scallop-and-mushroom cream version was reported at ¥850. Cream sauces here are flour-thickened.

items.en: Hayashi rice — beef and onion in a dark demi-glace stew over rice
items.note: Appears on the lunch rotation. Demi-glace is a wheat roux.
Advertised on a board outside; ¥700–¥730 depending on the day. Locals fill the place for it. Fried dishes such as the prawn-cutlet-and-white-fish set turn up on the rotation.

items.ja: エビカツと白身魚のフライ定食
items.romaji: ebikatsu to shiromizakana no furai teishoku
items.en: Prawn cutlet and white-fish fry set meal
items.note: Breadcrumbed and deep-fried; panko is wheat.
Reviewers call it generously filled; also served as one of the three morning-set choices with salad.
Until 11am, every day including Sunday. From about ¥520 — you pay for the drink and add ¥120 for the toast/sandwich/roll set; with a ¥380 blend coffee that lands at ¥500.
One of the morning-set options.
Wheat-batter crêpes with a drink.

items.ja: 自家製カスタードプリン
items.note: The most-photographed thing in the shop — a tall, firm old-school baked custard. Reported at ¥570 in an older review and ¥700 recently; ¥550 more for a drink set.
American coffee about ¥500 in a morning set.
Reported anywhere from ¥200 as part of a meal to ¥350 on its own.
Kansai kissaten staple — banana and tinned fruit blended with milk.

Kezurihi is the word for shaved ice used in Sei Shonagon's Pillow Book — the shop uses the old reading deliberately and names every flavour after a figure from Nara-period history. This is the shop's whole summer identity; flavours below are the individual bowls.
'Ichibiko' is the archaic Japanese word for strawberry.
Named for the princess who became Empress Jito; a blue syrup meant to evoke the water of Yoshino.

Named for Prince Oama (later Emperor Tenmu). Kuzu-mochi is arrowroot-starch jelly; kinako is roasted soybean flour. Ask whether the kuzu is 100% hon-kuzu — cheaper versions are cut with potato starch.
Otomo no Tabito wrote the Manyoshu's famous plum-blossom poems. Contains alcohol.

items.en: Blood orange and liqueur shaved ice ('grown-up' version)
items.note: Eukashi is a chieftain from the Emperor Jimmu legend. Contains alcohol.
Named for the Soga clansman assassinated in 645; sumomo is Japanese plum.
Prince Nagaya's Nara mansion site is a short walk away. Honey and dairy.
Named for the Nara court lady whose surname Tachibana means citrus.
Saohime is the goddess of spring in Nara's Saho hills.

items.en: Clove and loquat-leaf tea shaved ice
items.note: Chujo-hime is the Nara noblewoman of the Taima-dera mandala legend; loquat-leaf tea was a medieval medicinal drink.
Named after ancient tube-and-comma beads; topped with jelly pieces shaped like them. Ask whether the jelly is agar or gelatin.
Taishokkan was the highest court rank, granted to Fujiwara no Kamatari. Contains cheesecake, so wheat and dairy.
Kashikiya-hime is Empress Suiko. Yamato-toki is a Nara-grown medicinal root with a strong herbal flavour.

items.en: Kohaku-to crystal candy and vanilla ice cream shaved ice
items.note: Named for the princess who became Empress Gensho — her name literally contains the character for 'ice'. Kohaku-to is agar jelly dried to a crisp sugar shell.

items.ja: 古代のスイーツ（さくべい・まがり）とドリンクのセット
items.romaji: kodai no suiitsu (sakubei / magari) to dorinku no setto
items.en: Ancient-sweets set (sakubei and magari) with a drink
items.note: Reconstructions of karagashi — Tang-dynasty sweets recorded in Nara-period documents. Sakubei is a twisted rope of dough and magari a ring; both are wheat dough, fried. Genuinely the oldest identifiable confectionery in Japan.
Arrowroot-starch jelly from a Yoshino maker — Yoshino is the historic source of Japan's best kudzu. Clear, wobbly, eaten with kinako and syrup. Ask whether it is 100% hon-kuzu.

items.ja: 卵・牛乳不使用のホットケーキ
items.note: Made without egg or dairy — a rare find in a Japanese cafe — but still wheat flour. Paused during the busy shaved-ice season.

items.ja: メリメロベーキングさんのカヌレ
items.note: Bought in from a local baker. Paused during the shaved-ice season.
Milk boiled down for hours until it sets into a fudge-like block. Recorded as a tribute food in 8th-century Nara and revived from those records; tastes like unsweetened condensed milk.

items.ja: 須恵器でおつまみ（鴨・栗・蘇）
items.en: Snack plate served in Sue-ware (duck, chestnut, so)
items.note: Sueki is the grey unglazed stoneware of the Kofun and Nara periods; the shop serves the snacks in it.

items.ja: コーヒー・カフェオレ
items.note: Café au lait contains dairy.
Black tea made from Japanese tea leaves — milder and sweeter than Indian black tea.
Yuzu citrus preserved in sugar, dissolved in hot water; some brands use honey.
Ume syrup; the non-alcoholic version.
Beer is barley. Sake is rice-brewed but the koji handling is not declared.

items.ja: ホットコーヒー（中深煎り）
items.note: The whole point of the place: a record-playing coffee house where ¥500 gets you a seat with no cover charge. Roast level is chosen at the counter.
One of the named single origins.
Contains dairy.
The house sweet, ordered by almost everyone alongside the coffee. 'Rare' cheesecake in Japan means unbaked and set with gelatin, on a crushed-biscuit base.
The baked version; rich and dense.
Ordered with the dark-roast coffee.

items.ja: ひとくちモナカ（2種セット）
items.en: Bite-size monaka wafer sweets, set of two
items.note: Monaka are crisp wafer shells filled with bean paste — the wafer is made from mochi rice, but the fillings here were raspberry-and-white-bean and walnut-and-sesame-bean. Ask about the shell.

items.ja: おばんざいセット（コース）
items.en: Obanzai set — five to seven small home-style dishes, served one at a time
items.note: This is how the shop works: you order the set and small bowls arrive in sequence, changing daily. Obanzai is Kansai everyday home cooking, not restaurant food. Dashi and soy sauce run through nearly all of it, so assume wheat and fish.

The proprietor holds a SAKE DIPLOMA qualification. There is no written sake list — every bottle on the shelves is orderable; say whether you want it chilled or warmed and what flavour you like, and she offers you candidates. She is a warm-sake specialist.

items.ja: 具材いっぱいの白和え
items.en: Shira-ae — vegetables dressed in mashed tofu and sesame
items.note: Tofu is pounded smooth with white sesame and sugar and used as a dressing. Usually seasoned with a little soy or dashi.

items.ja: 柿と鯛と赤カブのマリネ
items.romaji: kaki to tai to akakabu no marine
items.en: Persimmon, sea bream and red-turnip marinade
items.note: Persimmon is Nara's signature fruit and appears constantly on autumn menus here.

items.en: Chicken gizzard in sweet vinegar marinade
items.note: Nanbanzuke means fried then steeped in vinegar, soy and chilli — the frying dredge and the soy are both wheat.
Grated lotus root formed into dumplings in a dashi broth.
A Chinese-Japanese crossover typical of the kitchen — doubanjiang and soy sauce both carry wheat.

items.ja: あんぽ柿クリームチーズの天婦羅
items.en: Semi-dried persimmon and cream cheese tempura
items.note: Anpo-gaki is persimmon dried only part-way, so it stays soft and jammy. Tempura batter is wheat.

items.ja: 鰻と梨のカマンベール春巻き
items.romaji: unagi to nashi no kamanbeeru harumaki
items.en: Eel, pear and camembert spring roll
items.note: Spring-roll wrappers are wheat.

items.ja: わさび菜入りサーモンのなめろう
items.note: Namero is raw fish chopped on the board with miso and aromatics until it is almost a paste — a fisherman's dish. Miso can be barley-based.

items.ja: 牛スジとこんにゃくの筑前煮
items.en: Beef tendon and konnyaku simmered Chikuzen-style
items.note: Chikuzen-ni is root vegetables browned then simmered in soy and mirin.

items.ja: 玄米リゾット粕汁添え
items.note: Kasujiru is soup enriched with sake lees — the residue left after pressing sake. Mildly alcoholic and warming; a winter staple in this region.
Surinagashi is a vegetable puréed and thinned with dashi — served as the opening warm or cold bowl.
Grilled rice cake topped with salted, dried mullet roe — a Kyoto-style luxury snack for sake.

items.ja: ブルーチーズハムカツ
items.note: Served by the quarter. Panko-crumbed and fried.

items.ja: 大人のお子さまランチ
items.note: The signature. A children's-plate layout done properly for adults: chicken rice under an omelette, hamburg steak, a prawn fry, Napolitan spaghetti, salad and soup, with the custard pudding added for the full price. Lunchtime only. There is a cat-shaped version too.

items.ja: ひよこ豆のカレー（for vegan）
items.note: The shop labels this one 'for vegan' on its own menu — unusual in a Nara kissaten. Confirm the spice paste and any soy seasoning if you need it gluten-free.
Spice-based minced-chicken curry rather than Japanese roux, but confirm.
Poached chicken breast on rice with a spring-onion-and-ginger sauce, plus black soy and sweet chilli on the side, with soup. Paused in winter. Soy sauce is wheat.

Nara's own zoni: white miso broth with round mochi and root vegetables — and the local twist is that you pull the mochi out and dip it in kinako (sweet roasted soybean flour) before eating. Miso may be barley-based.

items.ja: きのこあんかけハンバーグ
items.note: A daily lunch special. Hamburg patties in Japan are bound with panko, and ankake sauce is soy-based and starch-thickened.
Served all year, not just summer. Around ¥1,000–¥1,500 depending on the flavour.

items.ja: アボカドミルクと木の実
items.note: Seasonal. Contains dairy.

items.ja: ラズベリーミルク・ピスタチオ
items.en: Raspberry milk and pistachio shaved ice

items.ja: 喫茶店の苺ミックスジュースかき氷
items.romaji: kissaten no ichigo mikkusu juusu kakigori
items.note: Built to taste like the old kissaten mixed fruit juice.
Also served as 抹茶ミルクあずき with sweet red beans.

items.ja: 黒蜜きなこぷりんかき氷
items.en: Brown-sugar syrup, kinako and pudding shaved ice
items.note: Kuromitsu is unrefined-sugar syrup; kinako is roasted soybean flour.

items.ja: パンプキンチャイかき氷
items.note: Autumn flavour.
The shop's pudding, decorated as a black cat. Plain custard is wheat-free by recipe but the kitchen fries and bakes.
There is also an omurice morning set.
From 5pm the front room becomes a sake bar under a different name. Seen: aosa-seaweed potato salad, simmered kombu strips with fried tofu, and Okinawan shima-rakkyo with miso.
Narazuke is Nara's signature pickle — melon or gourd cured for months in sake lees. It is genuinely alcoholic and strongly so; not for drivers or children. Paired here with rich monkfish liver.

items.ja: 日本酒（奈良の地酒中心・14種）
items.en: Sake — about 14 kinds, mostly Nara breweries
items.note: Nara is where sake brewing as we know it was formalised, in the temple breweries of Shoryaku-ji. Shochu, gin and whisky are also poured.
Simmered in dashi and soy; fish-cake items contain wheat.

items.ja: 白子とほうれん草のキッシュ
items.note: Shirako is cod milt — creamy and mild. Pastry is wheat.

items.ja: カトゥレット（スリランカのコロッケ）
items.note: Deep-fried spiced fish-and-potato balls; breadcrumbed.

The shop's flagship, and its allergen line lists none of the eight major allergens. Fine wasanbon sugar pressed into thin tablets that dissolve on the tongue. Named by Prince Arisugawa after 'aoni-yoshi', the fixed poetic epithet for the city of Nara itself. Price is for a 5-piece box; ¥4,600 for 10, ¥8,300 for 18.
Ten smaller tablets. Allergen line: none declared.
The same sugar cake with sesame worked in. The shop declares sesame as the only allergen.

Modelled on the paper camellias the monks make for Todaiji's Omizutori rite each March, and invented by this shop — many imitations exist. Shop's allergen line: egg only. Two-day shelf life; sold only in season, 3 pieces for ¥2,890.
Named for the holy water drawn from the Wakasa well during Todaiji's Omizutori. Sold in assortments with the Roben camellia. Two-day shelf life; no allergens declared.

items.en: Kuzu-zakura — bean paste in arrowroot jelly
items.note: Red bean paste wrapped in translucent kudzu (arrowroot) starch jelly and a salted cherry leaf. Yoshino in southern Nara is Japan's classic source of kudzu. Shop declares no allergens. Six pieces ¥1,350.
Named for Asuka, the capital before Nara. A gentle salt note to cut the sweetness; 30-day shelf life. Shop declares no allergens. Nine pieces ¥1,500.
Crisp rice-flour wafers shaped as deer, filled with the shop's own bean paste — the deer of Nara Park were revered as messengers of the gods. Shop declares no allergens. Five pieces ¥2,100.
Purple, white, red, yellow and green — the five colours of the banners hung across great temple halls. Six sheets ¥2,160. No allergens declared.
An assortment of moulded dry sugar sweets whose shapes change with the season; made for the tea ceremony. Ten pieces ¥2,200. No allergens declared.

items.en: Kenjo Mikasa — large dorayaki-style bean-paste pancake
items.note: 'Mikasa' is the Kansai word for dorayaki, named after Nara's Mount Mikasa which the round cakes resemble. Shop's allergen line: wheat flour and egg. One piece ¥1,550.

items.en: Small Mikasa with the crane brand mark
items.note: A more manageable size, branded with the shop's standing-crane crest. Allergens: wheat flour, egg. Five pieces ¥2,200.

items.en: Yumedono — octagonal sweet after Horyu-ji's Hall of Dreams
items.note: Shaped after the octagonal Yumedono at Horyu-ji, associated with Prince Shotoku. Allergens: wheat flour, egg. Six pieces ¥3,000.
Despite 'senbei' usually meaning rice crackers, the shop's own allergen line reads wheat flour and egg — these are the wheat-flour kind. Eight packs ¥1,620.
Rustic old-Yamato flavour. Allergens declared by the shop: wheat flour, egg and peanut. Eight pieces in a bag ¥1,188.
The Portuguese-derived honey sponge cake. Allergens: wheat flour, egg. Sold by length — three sun (about 9cm) ¥3,600 up to six sun ¥7,200.
The castella batter rolled. Allergens: wheat flour, egg. Small ¥2,070, large ¥4,140.
A boxed pairing of Kyokusui-no-en and Asuka-kokyo. Allergens: wheat flour, egg.
Summer jelly sweets, 60-day shelf life. Six pieces ¥2,538. No allergen line published for this one — ask.

items.ja: 風味・3色・貝中しるこ
items.en: Instant shiruko — sweet red-bean soup in a wafer shell
items.note: A wafer shell you drop in a bowl and pour hot water over; it collapses into sweet red-bean soup. The 'kaichu' version comes in a clam-shaped shell. No allergen line published — ask about the wafer.

items.en: 'Yoshino River sweetfish' — bean-paste sweet in fish form
items.note: A summer sweet shaped as an ayu, the river fish caught in the Yoshino. Allergens: wheat flour, egg. Availability has been intermittent — ask.
Roasted by the method the founding owner used, still followed. Prices start around ¥400.
The thing people come for, and a remarkable ¥150 — but it cannot be ordered on its own; you must order a drink with it.
Described in a guidebook as idiosyncratic. Japanese curry roux is wheat-based.

items.ja: ビール＆おつまみセット
items.note: The place looks like an izakaya from outside and a machiya inside; beer with one snack is a set at ¥900. Beer is barley.
Changes weekly: a sandwich on the wife's home-baked wild-yeast bread, three side dishes and a soup. The shop name huerto is Spanish for kitchen garden and much of the veg comes from their own plot.

items.en: Pa amb tomàquet — bread rubbed with tomato and garlic
items.note: The Catalan classic, here topped with sheep's cheese and jamón. Bread is wheat.

items.ja: まぐろのコンフィときゅうりマリネサンド
items.romaji: maguro no konfi to kyuuri marine sando
items.en: Tuna confit and marinated cucumber sandwich
items.note: With soup and three sides. The weekly sandwich rotates — a chicken sauté with cumin-marinated cabbage version was also ¥1,300.
Around five kinds for two people. Seen: boiled whelks, tortilla, 23-month jamón serrano, pickled Jerusalem artichoke, vinegar-cured mackerel, smoked chicken.

items.ja: キタアカリのトルティージャ
items.note: Thick potato-and-egg omelette. Kita-akari is a sweet, floury Japanese potato variety. Also made with spinach.
The owner carves it at the counter; a 23-month-aged serrano and an Ibérico aged three years have both been on.

items.en: Pulpo a la gallega — octopus with paprika and olive oil
items.note: Boiled octopus, potato, smoked paprika, oil and salt.
Simmered in garlic oil in a terracotta dish; also done with sweet shrimp. The bread served alongside is wheat.
Shirako is cod milt — soft and custardy inside a fried coat. Batter is wheat.

items.ja: 紫とうがらしの素揚げ パドロン風
items.note: Whole small peppers fried plain and salted — a couple in every batch bite back. Shared fryer, so confirm for coeliac.

items.ja: 奈良県産 極太白ネギの藁焼き ロメスコソース
items.romaji: Nara-kensan gokubuto shironegi no warayaki romesuko soosu
items.en: Straw-grilled thick Nara leek with romesco
items.note: The Catalan calçot done with a fat Nara-grown white leek, charred over burning straw and served with the almond-and-pepper romesco. Confirm the romesco has no bread thickener.

items.ja: 自家製鶏のレバーパテ
items.note: Served with the house bread.

items.ja: 穴子とアサリのバスク風煮込み サルサヴェルデ
items.romaji: anago to asari no Basuku-fuu nikomi sarusa verude
items.en: Conger eel and clams in Basque salsa verde
items.note: Available as a half portion. Basque salsa verde is parsley, garlic and the shellfish liquor thickened with the fish's own gelatin — but flour is sometimes used, so ask.

items.ja: 車海老の海鮮パエリア
items.note: Also made with squid ink, and with scabbard fish and tomato. Rice-based; confirm the stock.
Baked by the owner's wife; reviewers single it out. Wheat.
Non-alcoholic.

items.en: Wine by the glass, red and white
items.note: Spanish list — a Garnacha Tintorera from Almansa and a Rueda white (Basa) have both been poured. Fining agents mean wine is not automatically vegan.

items.ja: 冷蔵庫の小鉢（オール300円）
items.note: How this bar works: a fridge of prepared small bowls that you take yourself and declare to the counter, every one ¥300. Contents change daily.
Coarsely crushed potato with ham and cucumber. Japanese mayonnaise contains egg.

items.en: Persimmon and cheese in mashed-tofu dressing
items.note: Shira-ae is tofu pounded with sesame into a dressing; persimmon is Nara's fruit. Rich enough to hold up to sake.

items.ja: スナップエンドウとコーンの白和え
items.romaji: sunappu endou to koon no shiraae
items.en: Snap pea and corn in mashed-tofu dressing
items.note: Tofu and white sesame, smooth; ask about dashi in the dressing.
The owner's family are fishermen in Amakusa, Kumamoto, and fish is sent up direct — about six species a day. A five-kind plate is also offered. The soy sauce served with it is wheat.
Seen: red grouper (akou), seared isaki, and sea bream.
Fugu cut in chunks rather than the thin fan — cheaper and chewier.
Creamy cod milt brushed with soy and grilled, finished with fried onion for crunch. Soy sauce is wheat.
Marinated in soy and dredged in starch — soy is wheat and fryers are shared.
Small sticky taro corms fried whole — a reviewer called them dangerously moreish.

items.ja: カニカマコロ（クリーム）
items.note: The crab-cream croquette done with surimi crab sticks. Panko and a flour béchamel.
Tempura batter is wheat.

items.en: Rolled omelette with spicy cod roe
items.note: Rolled dashi omelette, fluffy, with mentaiko inside and grated daikon alongside. A plain dashimaki is also on. Dashi seasoning normally contains soy.

items.ja: たっぷり野菜のトマト煮

items.note: The owner's own passion; the list is wide and rotates. Seen: Kitajima junmai ginjo origarami from Shiga, and Ruri momoiro muroka nama from Gunma, which ferments pink from a wild yeast.
From the only distillery on Amakusa, where the owner's family fish. Rice-based rather than the sweet-potato shochu Kyushu is known for; drunk on the rocks with food.

items.ja: パッション カマンベール
items.note: Motobu passionfruit and acerola against brown-sugar and custard syrups. Contains dairy.
The house bowl, named after the owner's dog — which is also the shop's name and is usually on the premises, so worth knowing if you are allergic to dogs.

items.en: Kotoka strawberry and mango shaved ice
items.note: Two sauces poured side by side — Kotoka is Nara's own strawberry variety. Hidden inside is a layer of green ice flavoured with fuchiba, Okinawan mugwort, which is more fragrant and less bitter than the mainland kind, and it is finished with crumbled chinsuko (Okinawan shortbread — wheat).
Shima-dofu is the dense, firm Okinawan tofu. Tiramisu means mascarpone and usually sponge — ask.
A vivid blue bowl meant to recall the Okinawan sea; uruma is an old poetic name for the islands.
The shop's simplest loaf: Hokkaido organic stone-ground wholemeal, Nara-grown wholemeal, organic yeast and salt. Nothing else. Shop declares no allergens for this one, but it is wheat.
A wider, chewier crumb than the rustique. Half loaves available. No allergens declared beyond the wheat itself.
Organic raisins, figs and whatever other fruit and nuts the baker fancies. Shop declares walnut. Half loaves available.

items.ja: ドライトマトとオリーブのバトン
items.romaji: dorai tomato to oriibu no baton
items.en: Semi-dried tomato and black olive baton
items.note: Italian semi-dried tomatoes. No allergens declared.

items.en: 'Deer antler' — apple and cream cheese twist
items.note: Named for Nara's deer; the dough is twisted into an antler shape. Shop declares walnut; contains cream cheese.

items.ja: ゴルゴンゾーラくるみ Bioはちみつ
items.note: Shop declares dairy and walnut; honey rules it out for vegans.
70% organic cacao. Shop declares dairy and walnut.

items.ja: 自家製ベーコンと生胡椒
items.en: House bacon and fresh green peppercorn
items.note: Fresh green peppercorns still on the stem — bright and citrussy rather than hot.

items.ja: ラムレーズンクリーム
items.note: Organic raisins steeped in rum with Yotsuba cream cheese. Shop declares dairy; contains alcohol.

Organic yeast, Nara wholemeal, Hokkaido wheat, Tanegashima unrefined sugar and Tokushima salt — and note it is a rounded rugby-ball loaf, not the square kaku-shoku most Japanese bakeries sell. No allergens declared.
The big loaf shrunk to one-person size.
Shop declares walnut.
Organic raisins, generously. Half loaves available.
Custard cooked with free-range eggs from the foot of Mt Katsuragi and unrefined sugar. Shop declares dairy and egg.
Made with Murasaki-sayaka azuki beans cooked in-house. No allergens declared beyond the wheat.
A whole free-range egg with house mayonnaise. Shop declares dairy and egg.
Natural cheese and Gruyère. Half loaves available. Shop declares dairy.
Piled with onion and house mayonnaise. Shop declares dairy and egg.
Melon pan is a bun under a crisp cookie crust — nothing to do with melon, it just looks like one. This version has wheat germ in the crust. Shop declares dairy and egg.
Shop declares dairy, egg and walnut.
Moist and chewy with roasted potato and salt. No allergens declared beyond the wheat.

The shop's own site calls this its founding signature — a proprietary method giving a chewy crumb that gets sweeter the more you chew. Price quoted is a five-slice pack; a 'zeitaku' (luxury) loaf sells at the same price.
Yamato-cha is Nara's own tea, grown in the eastern highlands since the 9th century when Kukai is said to have brought seeds back from China. Paired here with sweet bean paste and condensed milk.
The shop's most-photographed pastry; a nut version runs ¥280.
Curry filling in a breadcrumbed, deep-fried bun — the standard Japanese bakery item. Reported ¥230–¥260.
Shio-pan: a roll with a butter core that melts out and fries the base as it bakes. A plain shio-pan runs ¥130.

items.ja: クリームブリュレクイニーアマン
items.note: Kouign-amann is the Breton butter-and-sugar pastry with a caramelised base.

items.ja: バター香る濃厚キャラメルメロンパン
items.note: Melon pan is a bun under a crisp cookie shell — no melon involved.
Reported ¥180 + tax in an older post and ¥260 more recently.
There is also a chewy cinnamon doughnut at ¥220.

items.ja: 和風チキンフィレバーガー
炭焼きチキンの醤油マヨ
items.note: Soy sauce is wheat.
Croissant dough pressed in a waffle iron; a Korean street-food craze.

items.ja: 季節のデニッシュ（モンブラン・イチゴ）
items.en: Seasonal danish — Mont Blanc or strawberry
items.note: Named on the shop's own site as its seasonal specials.

items.ja: チェリーアーモンドタルト
items.note: One of the shop's named recommendations.
From the shop's own new-product announcement. Okonomiyaki sauce is wheat-based.
From the shop's own new-product announcement. Miso can be barley-based.

items.en: 'Baguewassant' — salt croissant made from baguette dough
items.note: The shop's best-known item: croissant shape, baguette dough, French cultured butter and Guérande salt, so it comes out crunchy-then-chewy rather than flaky. Reported ¥280–¥330 over time; a matcha version runs ¥500.
Sold whole or half. The shop suggests reheating it briefly and eating it with wine.

items.ja: 奈良漬けチーズチャバタ
items.note: Narazuke is Nara's sake-lees pickle — melon or gourd buried in the lees left from brewing for months. It is genuinely alcoholic, so not for drivers or children; here its yeasty tang is mellowed by Gouda.

items.ja: チャバタ 花山椒くるみ
items.en: Ciabatta with sansho flower and walnut
items.note: Two kinds of sansho (Japanese pepper), red and green — numbing and citrussy rather than hot. Contains walnut.

items.ja: チャバタ マロングラッセ
白味噌とカシューナッツのチャバタ
items.romaji: shiromiso to kashuu nattsu no chabata
items.note: White miso is normally rice-koji, but confirm — some miso is barley.
French flour, crackling crust, chewy inside. Also made up as a croque-monsieur with ginger jam and ham.

items.en: Melon pan with white bean paste
items.note: Melon pan is a bun under a crisp sugared cookie crust and contains no melon. What makes this one different is the white bean paste hidden inside.
Brown sugar and French butter, Breton style — shattering outside, dense and buttery inside.
House custard, vanilla-scented.
French flour and French butter. An apple version runs ¥520.
Two Valrhona batons inside.
Four pieces per bag. Literally 'lost bread' — day-old bread soaked in custard and baked.

items.ja: 奈良のほうじ茶あんぱん
items.note: Hojicha is green tea roasted until it turns brown and smoky.

items.ja: 玉葱と蓮根生姜焼きのホットドッグ
items.romaji: tamanegi to renkon shougayaki no hottodoggu
items.en: Onion and ginger-fried lotus-root hot dog
items.note: Shogayaki sauce is soy-based, so wheat twice over.

items.ja: ケイクオルヴァン 抹茶と柚子
items.romaji: keiku oru van maccha to yuzu
items.en: Cake au vin with matcha and yuzu
items.note: A loaf cake meant to be eaten with wine.
Thick, salty-buttery Breton shortbread.
The bakery's take on the mochi sweet, in bread form.
The shop also does take-away drinks.

items.ja: おまかせ前菜5種の盛り合わせ
items.note: The way most people begin here. One recorded plate: vegetable pickles, confit gizzard, roast duck, venison stew, chickpea hummus and grissini (grissini are wheat).
A short tasting run for one person.

items.ja: 自家製ベーコングリル
items.note: Cured on the premises.

items.ja: 軽くソテーした自家製スモークサーモン サラダ添え
items.romaji: karuku sotee shita jikasei sumooku saamon sarada-zoe
items.en: Lightly sautéed house-smoked salmon with salad

items.ja: ブルーチーズのクリームパスタ
items.note: Wheat pasta.
Simmered in garlic oil; the bread served alongside is wheat.

items.ja: 焼き茄子と魚のタルタル

items.note: Shirayaki means grilled with no sauce — just salt — so unlike the usual glazed eel this one has no soy on it. Confirm what is served with it.
Stewed summer vegetables; confirm no butter or stock for vegan.

items.ja: ゴルゴンゾーラと紅芋と紅玉りんごのケークサレ
items.romaji: gorugonzoora to beniimo to kougyoku ringo no keeku sale
items.en: Gorgonzola, purple sweet potato and Kogyoku apple cake salé
items.note: Cake salé is a savoury loaf cake — wheat.

items.ja: 本日のクレームブリュレ
items.note: Custard under burnt sugar; wheat-free by recipe but ask about the kitchen.
Beer is barley.

items.ja: 日本ワイン・フランスワイン
items.note: The reason the bar exists — a list weighted to Japanese domestic bottles alongside French. Wine is often fined with animal products, so not automatically vegan.

items.ja: フェアトレードコーヒーのセット
items.note: The core of the place: fair-trade coffee served in what is essentially a private house fitted out as a small live-music room. Price from a 2019 visit. The sweet that comes with it is usually a cookie, so wheat.
The menu names it explicitly as fair-trade.
Umaji is a tiny Kochi mountain village famous nationwide for its yuzu. Some yuzu preserves are made with honey.
Small baked sweets served with the coffee; a visitor on a hot day was given chocolate balls and cookies for free.
The house signature and a pun — shikaku sounds like 'assassin' but is written to suggest a knockout plate. The owner buys at market daily; the photo price is for two. Soy sauce is wheat.
The most-ordered lunch item; the surface is blowtorched and the centre left raw.
Tuna crumbed and fried so the middle stays rare. Panko is wheat.
¥800–¥1,000 for most days, with rice, miso soup, a small side, pickles and coffee — and sometimes cake. Rice and soup are refillable. A Hokkaido wild yellowtail lunch was ¥1,480.
The shop makes a point of wild rather than farmed fish. Also served grilled over charcoal at ¥980, or as teriyaki.
Winter dish — paper-thin yellowtail swished through hot broth for a second so it only just turns opaque. Photo price is for two.
Market price, reservation required. Tecchiri is the Osaka word for fugu hotpot; kue is a prized deep-water grouper.
Harihari-nabe is an old Osaka dish — whale meat with mizuna greens, named for the crunching sound the greens make. Whale is also served as sashimi (¥1,100), cutlet (¥1,200) and with ginger (¥1,200).
Miso may be barley-based.
Tofu warmed in kombu broth and dipped in ponzu — the ponzu contains soy sauce, and the broth here is unlikely to be meat-free.
Yokowa is the Kansai name for juvenile bluefin — leaner and cheaper than adult maguro.
A slender silver spring fish with a needle-like lower jaw.
Shirako is cod milt — creamy and rich. Ponzu contains soy sauce. A tempura version is ¥950.
Panko-crumbed. Oysters also served with vinegar (¥750) or with butter (¥800).
A butter version is ¥650. Sake-steamed clams are usually just sake, salt and clams — but confirm no soy.
Tempura batter is wheat and the fryer is shared with fish.
A house favourite — large portions on request, and they will bring you a pot of dashi to pour over the leftovers and finish it as ochazuke. Eel glaze and fried rice both use soy.
Tiny whole fish dried a single night and grilled — eaten head and all.
Salt-grilled whole over charcoal. Sawara (Spanish mackerel) is ¥790 and salted mackerel ¥690.

items.ja: 花しばトマトソースパスタ
items.note: The 'creative' half of the shop's name. Wheat pasta.
Usually topped with bonito flakes and a soy dressing — ask.

Three regional versions are offered — Chengdu, rustic Deyang and Chongqing — and heat is chosen from five levels. Price is for the set meal. Doubanjiang bean paste and soy sauce both contain wheat, and it has pork in it.
Poached chicken under Sichuan chilli oil, sesame and numbing sansho. The sauce is soy-based.

items.ja: もちもち厚皮のゆで餃子
items.note: The shop leans on the chew of the thick wrapper rather than a fried base; choose Sichuan sesame sauce or a Japanese-style dip. Wrappers are wheat.
Wheat wrappers holding hot broth — bite carefully.
Wheat wrappers, deep-fried.

items.ja: おまかせMIXカルパッチョ
items.note: The 'creative' side of this kitchen — one plate held botan shrimp, Tsugaru-strait salmon, lean tuna, tuna neck meat, horse mackerel and ark shell. Confirm the dressing for soy.

items.ja: 剣先イカの生ウニ和え
items.en: Swordtip squid dressed with raw sea urchin
items.note: Squid from Shimane, sliced fine so it turns sticky-sweet, folded through fresh uni.

items.ja: 豚バラ肉自家製チャーシュー
items.en: House char siu of pork belly
items.note: Skin left on so it turns gelatinous; served with a sweet glaze and mustard. Soy-based glaze.

items.ja: 唐辛子麺でスタミナラーメン
items.note: Cabbage and pork fried hard with garlic and chilli, given depth with fermented black bean, on chilli-kneaded noodles. Ramen noodles are wheat.
Wheat noodles in a soy-based broth.

items.en: Sara udon — crisp noodles under seafood gravy
items.note: Nagasaki dish: noodles fried until they shatter, then drowned at the table in a thick vegetable-and-seafood sauce.

items.en: Seafood sauce over crisp scorched rice
items.note: Black-rice okoge fried until it crackles, then the hot sauce is poured over it at the table so it hisses. Sauce is soy-thickened.

items.en: Taiwanese braised pork belly rice (lu rou fan)
items.note: Pork belly stewed with soy, rice wine and star anise, with coriander. Soy sauce is wheat.
Weekday lunch: fried rice with salt pork, plus boiled gyoza, chicken soup and sesame-oil pickles.
Hokkaido cod milt under cheese and sauce — flour-thickened.
Chinese rice wine — but fermented with a wheat-based starter, so not gluten-free. By the glass or bottle.
Four times the bitterness of standard Tsingtao. Beer is barley.

items.ja: 和菓子と飲み物のセット
items.note: This is essentially the whole menu — a wagashi and a drink, served on the shop's antique tableware, which is the point of visiting. What the sweet is changes.

items.en: Monaka — bean paste in a crisp wafer shell
items.note: Served on an antique crane-motif dish. Monaka wafers are made from mochi rice, but ask — some are blended with wheat.

items.ja: アイス珈琲とメロンシャーベットのセット
items.romaji: aisu koohii to meron shaabetto no setto
items.note: A summer-only set. Sherbet usually contains dairy.

Amuse, starter of the day, a pasta, a main, dessert and coffee. Prices on the shop's site are stated before tax. First-time guests must order a course — à la carte is only offered at the counter on repeat visits.
Adds a seasonal course between the starter and the pasta.
Amuse, starter, pasta, main, then your pick of cheese, dessert or a second pasta, plus dessert and coffee.
Adds separate fish and meat courses.
Reservation required.

The kitchen makes everything itself — pasta, bread, prosciutto, salami, anchovies, bottarga, even the limoncello. Meat and fish arrive whole and are butchered on site. Fresh pasta is wheat and usually egg.

items.ja: 自家製生ハム・サラミ
items.note: Cured in the restaurant.
The owner holds a hunting licence and goes out in season, so what he shoots can appear on the plate. Ask what is on.

items.ja: オードブル（テイクアウト）
items.note: From ¥2,500 per head — around twenty items including house charcuterie, lasagne and Italian deli dishes.
From ¥6,000 per head: starter platter, pasta, main, bread and dessert.
Sparkling, white, red, beer, sake, cocktails and soft drinks. Beer is barley.

items.ja: イタリアワイン（100種以上）
items.note: Plus house limoncello and spumante as aperitifs, grappa and calvados after. Wine is often animal-fined.
A 1945-founded neighbourhood Chinese restaurant on the Higashimuki arcade. Lunch has held at ¥880 for years.

items.en: Set meal with your choice of main
items.note: Six mains to choose from — karaage, sweet-and-sour pork, happosai, stir-fried vegetables, crab omelette or chilli shrimp — each set with soup, spring roll and pickles. ¥1,000 or ¥1,200 depending on the main; served at dinner too.
A fluffy crab-and-egg omelette under a sweet-vinegar starch sauce. Sauce is soy-based.
Not a Chinese dish at all despite the name — a Japanese invention. This one is unusually loaded with bamboo shoot, carrot and bok choy under the egg. Sauce is soy-based.

items.en: Chuka-don — stir-fried vegetables and seafood over rice
items.note: Set with spring roll and soup. Gentle starch-thickened sauce; soy-based.
Available as a set or as a donburi. Doubanjiang and soy sauce are both wheat; contains pork.
Ketchup-and-chilli sauce with a distinct kick. Reported ¥1,080 as a set.
The classic build — onion, green pepper, bamboo shoot and carrot; the shop's version arrives on a 20cm oval plate. A small single portion exists.
Mixed vegetables, pork and seafood in a light starch sauce.
Fragrant with five-spice; comes with corn soup, a mini spring roll and zha cai pickle. Soy marinade and shared fryer.
Prawn, scallop and squid with broccoli and baby corn, salt-seasoned.
Lettuce added at the last second so it stays crunchy. Plain fried rice tops it with small shrimp. Soy seasoning.

items.en: Crisp fried noodles under vegetable gravy
items.note: Noodles fried until brittle, then buried in prawn, wood-ear, cabbage, carrot, bean sprout and pepper gravy.
Clean salt broth with scallop, prawn and squid.
Soy broth with a thickened sauce that keeps it scalding to the last mouthful.
Strongly seasoned, meant to be eaten with rice.
With cucumber, water chestnut and onion.
Sold by the portion; two portions is a normal order. Wrappers are wheat. Boiled dumplings also offered.
Duck egg cured in alkaline clay until the white turns to dark jelly. Strong and ammoniac — an acquired taste.

items.ja: 胡麻団子と杏仁プリン
items.note: Goma dango are glutinous-rice balls rolled in sesame and fried; annin-dofu is set with milk. The fryer is shared with wheat items.

About ¥1,800 a head (¥3,600 for two): egg soup, a cold starter of steamed chicken and spare ribs, spring roll, chilli shrimp, sweet-and-sour pork, fried rice and almond jelly. There is a 30-seat banquet room upstairs.
Comes with red miso soup. A 70-year-old Naramachi sushi counter with a live tank of horse mackerel and filefish. Soy sauce is wheat by default; ask for tamari if you need it.

One recorded plate: prawn, tamago, amberjack, salt-dressed swordtip squid, ikura, chutoro tuna, flounder with grated daikon and ponzu, simmered conger eel, seared scallop and red miso soup — the composition changes with the season. Cuts are on the large side.

items.en: Chirashi — sashimi scattered over sushi rice
items.note: A lunch option.
A lunch option. Tekka-maki (tuna roll) is also on the counter.
Yes, a sushi shop with udon — normal in an old Kansai neighbourhood restaurant. Udon is wheat.
Seen: gizzard shad, herring roe, squid and cockle. Also single plates of bluefin, amberjack, whelk and halfbeak.

items.en: Uzaku — grilled eel with vinegared cucumber
items.note: Rich grilled eel cut with sharp cucumber vinegar. Eel glaze is soy-based.
Early-summer river fish grilled whole on a skewer and eaten head to tail; the bitter guts are the point. Just salt.
Dashi-set egg custard with things hidden in it; the dashi is seasoned with soy.
Simmered in soy and mirin.
Winter delicacy — creamy cod milt with a soy glaze.
Autumn only. Matsutake and chicken steamed in a small clay teapot; you pour the broth into the lid-cup and drink it before eating the contents. The broth is soy-seasoned.
Salted, pressed and dried mullet roe, made in-house; intensely savoury, sliced thin for sake.
Salt-grilled Nagasaki and Tokushima beef have both been served.

items.en: Hirezake — hot sake with a toasted fugu fin
items.note: A dried pufferfish fin toasted and dropped into hot sake; it is set alight to burn off the alcohol vapour, then drunk. Smoky and savoury.

items.ja: 風の森 純米大吟醸
items.en: Kaze no Mori junmai daiginjo sake
items.note: From Yucho Shuzo in Gose, Nara — one of the most sought-after sake breweries in Japan, bottled unpasteurised and lively. Served in a green cup here.
Booked in the upstairs tatami rooms; a party of five reported ¥6,000 a head. The daily recommendations are chalked on a whiteboard without prices, so ask before ordering.

items.en: Omurice — chicken rice in a thin omelette
items.note: What almost everyone orders. The base version is old-fashioned: onion-and-mushroom ketchup chicken rice wrapped in a thin, fully-cooked egg sheet rather than the modern runny kind. Ketchup and stock cubes both commonly carry wheat.

items.ja: デミグラスソースのオムライス
items.note: Demi-glace is built on a wheat-flour roux.

items.ja: トマトソースのオムライス
明太子クリームソースのオムライス
