items.note: Price is before tax. Mentaiko is pollock roe cured with chilli; the cream sauce is flour-thickened.

items.ja: シーフードオムライス
items.note: Squid, prawn and scallop in tomato sauce.
You pick a side — cutlet, prawn fry or others. A board outside advertised omurice plus karaage or prawn fry at ¥940.

items.ja: 温泉卵とスモークチキンのカレードリア
items.romaji: onsen tamago to sumooku chikin no karee doria
items.en: Curry doria with smoked chicken and soft-cooked egg
items.note: Doria is rice under béchamel and cheese, baked. Both the béchamel and the Japanese curry roux are wheat.

items.ja: エビとブロッコリーのドリア
明太子クリームのパスタ
items.note: With shiso leaf and shredded nori — the Japanese-Italian hybrid ubiquitous in kissaten.
Teriyaki-glazed patty with salad — a cafe-style donburi. Patty is bound with panko and the glaze is soy.
A light option rather than a full meal.

items.ja: ベイクドチーズケーキ
items.note: The cakes in the display case are plated with a little work before serving.
Set with gelatin on a biscuit base.

items.ja: シフォンケーキセット
ケーキとドリンクのセット

items.note: Singled out by reviewers as unusually good for a cafe of this kind.

A shop founded in 1901 in the Mochiidono arcade that fries fish paste all day and sells it hot over the counter. IMPORTANT: the shop's own allergen line reads wheat, soy, dairy, prawn and peanut — so none of this is gluten-free. Prices below are the pre-tax single-piece prices from the shop's own site.
The shop's own number-one seller — fish paste around buttery potato.
Thick tentacles with a natural sweetness; a signature item.
Fish paste sandwiched between slices of Tsutsui lotus root — a Nara heirloom vegetable grown in Yamatokoriyama. A plain lotus sandwich with onion is ¥250.
Domestic wood-ear from Asuka village in Nara — all crunch.
Named after Nara's Mount Wakakusa; packed with Hokkaido sweetcorn. Also sold in a five-piece pack.
Nothing but fish paste, fried flat — the baseline against which everything else is judged.
The one that goes in oden.
Finely chopped squid through the paste.
Red pickled ginger keeps it light.
Roughly chopped onion, and a lot of it.
Burdock shaved into slivers the way you sharpen a pencil — earthy and fragrant. A rolled burdock version is ¥180.
Sold whole and sliced into rounds at home; a bento staple.
One entire prawn inside.

items.en: 'Mikasa' — kamaboko with prawn and spring onion
items.note: Named after Nara's Mount Mikasa.
Fish and green peas wrapped in fresh yuba — the skin that forms on heated soy milk.

items.en: Whole boiled egg in fish paste
items.note: An entire boiled egg encased and fried. Order in advance.
Quail eggs inside.
Isobe means 'seashore' — anything dressed in green nori.
Peeled shrimp, sakura shrimp and green laver.
Long stick-shaped cakes, all ¥480: kimchi, cheese, squid, whitebait, okonomiyaki-flavour and octopus.

items.en: Kamaboko — steamed fish cake on a board
items.note: The shop has made these for over 110 years. Steamed rather than fried, sliced and eaten cold with wasabi.

items.ja: さつま揚げ基本セット A
items.note: The set to buy if you have no idea where to start.

items.ja: 奈良の地酒とさつま揚げのセット「倭蔵」
items.romaji: Nara no jizake to satsuma-age no setto 'Wagura'
items.en: Nara sake and fish-cake gift set 'Wagura'
items.note: Paired with Harushika, one of Nara city's historic breweries.

items.ja: アイシングクッキー（オーダーメイド）
items.note: The shop's main trade — you commission the design. Its own ingredient statement reads Hokkaido wheat flour, Yotsuba butter and egg. Prices are per cookie and rise with complexity: 4–5cm letters and numbers ¥300, 8–9cm ¥600, animal shapes from ¥450, characters or logos ¥500–¥650.

items.ja: アイシングクッキー（店頭）
items.note: Seasonal sets sold over the counter in little bags — owls and autumn colours, Halloween, New Year zodiac animals. A small autumn set was reported at ¥850 before tax.
Small, round and unexpectedly thick — reviewers recommend these over the decorated ones for eating rather than gifting.

items.ja: チョコチップクッキー
items.note: Sold plain enough that you can draw a face on it yourself with a chocolate pen.

items.ja: ソルトバタークッキー

items.note: Narazuke is Nara's sake-lees pickle, worked into a cookie — the lees give it a boozy, yeasty depth. Contains alcohol.

The most interesting thing on the drinks side: a Taiwanese Hakka preparation that arrives as a powder of ground tea, soybean, yam and mixed grains. You add hot water and sweeten it with beet sugar; it comes out thick, savoury and nutty, more soup than tea. Ask about the grain blend — barley is common in these mixes.
Served in the shop with a cookie; the shop's Facebook shows teapot service with a small sweet.

items.ja: ホットサンドセット（Bセット）
items.note: The shop's centre of gravity. Choose one of three fillings; comes with a mini salad, crisps, a boiled egg and a drink. Priced as the drink plus about ¥300, so ¥550–¥700 depending on what you drink. The morning version is ¥500–¥650.

items.ja: ホットサンド ハム＆たまご
items.note: The one most reviewers name as the best of the three. Price is the in-set price.

items.ja: ホットサンド ハム＆チーズ
ホットサンド ツナ＆チーズ
もち＆あんこのホットサンド
items.romaji: mochi to anko no hotto sando
items.note: A Nagoya-style idea — rice cake and sweet bean paste pressed hot between bread.

items.ja: ベーコンとチーズのホットサンドモーニング
items.romaji: beekon to chiizu no hotto sando mooningu

items.ja: モーニングセット A
items.note: Toast, salad, egg and a drink, from 7am. There are three tiers at ¥550/¥650/¥700 depending on the drink; a plain version comes to ¥600.

items.ja: 牛スネ肉のカレーセット
items.note: 300g of rice with a drink and salad. Japanese curry roux is wheat.
Two sauces, maple and strawberry; the bread is soaked right through with egg. A strawberry version is also served.
The default set drink; anything else costs a supplement.
A ¥100 supplement in a set; flavoured lattes ¥150.
A ¥100 supplement in a set.

items.ja: 和牛ふわふわオムカレー
items.note: Listed on the menu as the number-one seller: a soft, buttery omelette over rice with the beef curry poured around it. Note that this shop traded until recently as 和牛スジカレー 奈良本店 (Wagyu Suji Curry) at the same address and the menu carried over; older prices you find online belong to that name. Japanese curry sauce is a wheat roux.
The dish the shop was originally named after — beef tendon stewed until it collapses. Large rice-and-sauce portion around ¥1,130 before tax.

items.ja: 和牛ごろごろビーフカレー
items.note: Whole blocks of beef rather than shreds. The shop is a sister to the teppanyaki restaurant Chez Bleu, which is where the meat quality comes from. An extra-large portion was reported at ¥1,870.

items.ja: 黒毛和牛ロースステーキカレー
items.note: The top of the range.
Prawn, scallop and squid in a lighter, fresher sauce, with coloured vegetables arranged over the rice — reviewers compare the presentation to a hotel restaurant.
The non-curry option — beef and onion in a dark demi-glace, which is also a wheat roux.

items.ja: 薬味（福神漬け・らっきょう・奈良漬・レーズン・激辛ソース）
items.note: Five accompaniments come with every plate, and the one worth noticing is the narazuke — melon cured in sake lees, Nara's own pickle, which almost nobody else serves with curry and which reviewers say works. Fukujinzuke and the chilli sauce are soy-based.
Sold as a set add-on; confirm the dressing.

items.ja: 自家製ケーキ（日替わり）
items.note: Baked by a pâtissière who also runs a small cake school on the premises. The cafe sits at the back of the Irie Taikichi Memorial Nara City Museum of Photography, looking onto the garden — and you do not need a museum ticket to use it.

items.ja: 自家製ケーキセット（ドリンク付）
items.en: Cake of the day with a drink

items.note: The kissaten standard — bread topped with tomato sauce, cheese and a slice of ham, grilled.
Contains dairy.
Contains dairy.

items.ja: ちょい奈寐（地酒3種＋つまみ3種）
items.en: 'Choi-Kamunabi' — three Nara sakes with three snacks
items.note: The signature set, and the reason to come: three Nara-brewed sakes with three small dishes. One recorded round was the dry Koryo-gura, the sweet Kingaku and the cloudy Hanatomoe, with enoki in persimmon dressing, simmered daikon, and ginger-and-tuna tsukudani. The sign outside says 'drinking from morning' and means it — the bar opens at 8am.
Served until 9:30. Non-guests are welcome.
Repeatedly singled out by reviewers as better than it has any right to be. Japanese mayonnaise contains egg.
Small sausages cut so the ends splay into tentacles when fried — a Japanese lunchbox classic, here served with beer.

items.ja: オーガニッククッキー
items.note: Oatmeal and raisin, with Earl Grey served in a pot. Oats are frequently cross-contaminated with wheat.
Made with milk.
Beer is barley.

items.ja: 日本酒（お猪口／ぐい飲み選択）
items.note: You pick your own ochoko or guinomi from the shelf. Wine, shochu and even Yomeishu medicinal liqueur are also poured.

items.ja: ラーメン・カレーライス
items.note: The proper-meal end of the menu. Ramen noodles and Japanese curry roux are both wheat.

items.ja: 奈良を味わうショートコース
items.note: The entry course at lunch, recommended for a first visit. The restaurant is a counter-only room for four parties at night — the chef cooks everything himself and won the 2021 national Italian cuisine competition.

items.ja: 奈良を味わうおまかせコース
items.note: The standard course, served at both services. Built on ingredients from Uda in eastern Nara, where the vegetables are organically grown.

items.ja: 奈良の記憶を刻むコース（昼）
items.romaji: Nara no kioku o kizamu koosu
items.en: 'Memory of Nara' course — eight dishes with cheese
items.note: The omakase plus a course of aged cheeses chosen by an affineur.

items.ja: 奈良の記憶を刻むコース（夜）
items.romaji: Nara no kioku o kizamu koosu (yoru)
items.en: 'Memory of Nara' dinner course — seven dishes
items.note: The most-booked course. Threads in what the restaurant calls 'Yamato Italian' — Italian technique applied to Nara's own food culture.

items.ja: 奈良の記憶を深めるコース
items.romaji: Nara no kioku o fukameru koosu
items.en: 'Deepening the memory of Nara' — eight dishes with cheese
items.note: The full evening.
A cheaper five-plate lunch listed on the restaurant's English booking page — worth asking about if the ¥8,000 course is more than you want.
The dish the restaurant names as its own: thick Tuscan hand-rolled pici in a sauce combining tomato and sauce américaine (a shellfish reduction). Wheat, and the sauce is shellfish-based.
Sourced through a trusted Hokkaido supplier.
Shipped direct from the port rather than via market, so it arrives a day fresher.

items.ja: 宇陀産オーガニック野菜
items.note: Uda is the highland district east of Nara city; its cold nights are why the vegetables taste as they do.

items.ja: イタリアワイン（ソムリエ・エクセレンス選定）
items.en: Italian wine chosen by a Sommelier Excellence
items.note: The owner's wife holds the Sommelier Excellence qualification, rare in Nara prefecture, and does the pairing. Wine is often animal-fined.

items.ja: おまかせ料理（ご予算に応じて）
items.en: Chef's choice cooking, to your budget
items.note: This is how the shop describes itself on the arcade's own page: tell them a budget and a professional cooks to it. From about ¥2,500 including drinks and karaoke. There is no fixed printed menu, so expect Japanese izakaya cooking built on soy and dashi.

A reviewer's pick of the shop — thigh meat brought to the table sizzling on iron with white leek and pepper. The owner's line is that it is ordinary supermarket chicken transformed by preparation and heat control. Sauces here are soy-based.
Soy marinade and shared fryer.
Wheat noodles in a dashi broth.
Not food, but it is half the reason people come — the shop advertises itself as 'drink, sing, eat' and stays open to midnight.

items.ja: 名物白金豚の肉豆腐（関西風）
items.en: Signature Hakkin pork and tofu hotpot, Kansai style
items.note: The shop's own line is 'if you don't eat this you haven't been here'. Silken tofu and Hakkin-ton pork simmered in a clay pot in a light dashi with unfiltered whole-soybean soy sauce. Soy sauce is wheat.

items.ja: 菜っ葉と薄あげのたいたん（大）
items.en: Greens and thin fried tofu, simmered
items.note: 'Taitan' is Kansai dialect for a simmered dish. Dashi here is made with bonito, kombu and dried sardine, so it is not vegetarian. Small size ¥350.

items.ja: ヤマトポークのチャーシュー（中）
items.note: Yamato Pork is Nara prefecture's own branded pork. Braised until it falls apart, deeply soaked in the soy braise. Small ¥480, large ¥1,150.

items.en: Fresh wheat-gluten cake with three misos
items.note: Namafu is raw wheat gluten — chewy, faintly sweet, a Kyoto-Nara temple food, and pure gluten, so absolutely not for coeliacs. Three colours of fu with three misos: sea-urchin miso, yuzu white miso and red miso.

items.en: 'Snow tiger' — grilled thick fried tofu with grated daikon
items.note: Atsuage grilled on a rack until it takes tiger stripes of char, buried under snow-white grated daikon. Said to have been a favourite of the artist-gourmet Rosanjin. Usually dressed with soy — ask.
Tofu buried in miso until it turns dense and cheese-like — a preserved food attributed to the Heike clan. Strongly salty and savoury, meant to be nibbled slowly with sake. Miso can be barley.

items.en: Bakurai — sea squirt with salted sea-cucumber gut
items.note: Two of Japan's most extreme sake foods combined: fermented sea-squirt shiokara and konowata, salted sea-cucumber intestine. Briny, funny-tasting, and much loved by sake drinkers.

items.en: Cod roe and shirataki with sansho
items.note: Cod roe cooked with konnyaku noodles and the citrus-numbing sansho pepper.
One of the choices for the compulsory otoshi (table snack, ¥200).

items.ja: 名物きゅうりの土佐漬け1本勝負
items.romaji: meibutsu kyuuri no Tosa-zuke ippon shoubu
items.note: 'Tosa' in a dish name always means bonito flakes. A whole cucumber, served as a challenge.
Add potato salad for ¥150. Dressings are usually soy- and egg-based.
Large ¥550.
Mashed taro wrapped around a core of rice cake and fried, so it stretches when you pull it apart. Available as a half portion. Shared fryer.

items.ja: 甘海老の唐揚げ 金砂粉まみれ
items.en: Fried sweet shrimp dusted in spiced crumb
items.note: Eaten shell and all, coated in a panko-and-sansho powder.
An Osaka classic — tendon cooked for hours in sweet miso until it turns to jelly. Also served over rice with a curry note at ¥800.
Split flat, dried a single night and grilled; the standard izakaya fish. Half fillet ¥650, bone-in ¥850. Salt only, but the soy you dress it with is wheat.
Small ¥480. Whole tiny fish, eaten head and bones.

items.ja: ビーフ紙カツ ソース味
items.note: Beef beaten thin as paper, crumbed and fried; tonkatsu sauce is wheat-based.

items.ja: 揚げえび春巻き（2本入り）
items.note: Prawn and white fish inside a wheat wrapper.

Tatsuta-age means marinated in soy and mirin then dredged in potato starch — the starch is fine but the soy is wheat. Named after the Tatsuta River in Nara, whose autumn maple leaves the reddish crust is meant to evoke.

items.ja: ぷるんぷるんのだし巻き玉子
items.note: Must be ordered by 2pm the same day. Egg rolled with a lot of dashi so it barely holds together.

items.en: Chilled green-tea soba with grated daikon
items.note: Cha-soba is buckwheat noodle kneaded with matcha — but it is always blended with wheat flour, and the dipping sauce is soy and dashi.

items.ja: 塩昆布と山椒の佃煮茶漬け
items.romaji: shiokonbu to sanshou no tsukudani chazuke
items.en: Rice in tea with salted kelp and sansho tsukudani
items.note: The classic way to finish a drinking night: hot tea or dashi poured over rice. The house-made sansho gives it a clean, tingling finish. Tsukudani is simmered in soy. Plain salted-kelp version ¥400.

items.ja: 有明産のり巻きおにぎり（2ヶ）
items.en: Rice balls in Ariake nori, two
items.note: Ariake Sea nori is the most prized in Japan. A version with ancient purple rice is ¥450, char-siu rice ¥630, chirimen-sansho rice ¥580, plain rice ¥200.

items.ja: 奈良の地酒 飲み比べセット
items.note: This was the first bar in Nara to commit entirely to Nara-brewed sake, and it still has rarities. One flight held Kuramoto Dry, Suinin no Sato from Umenoyado, and Hanatomoe.
The house original: shochu, fresh lime and ginger ale. Refreshing and easy.
Divisive: sweet, bitter, salty and metallic all at once. A serious sake food.

items.ja: トースト・たまごサラダ（モーニング）
items.en: Toast with egg salad, morning set
items.note: Opens at 8am, one minute from Kintetsu-Nara station. Every morning set is ¥530 and includes coffee or tea, hot or iced. Add-ons ¥50–¥80: mini salad, yoghurt, boiled egg, egg salad or sweet red bean.

items.ja: トースト・小倉（モーニング）
items.en: Toast with sweet red bean, morning set
items.note: Ogura toast is the Nagoya kissaten classic — butter, then a slab of sweet azuki paste.

items.ja: ハニートースト（モーニング）
items.note: The shop's own site names this as its morning signature alongside the egg hot dog.

items.ja: ピザトースト（モーニング）
ホットドッグ タマゴ
items.note: Comes with salad, yoghurt and a drink. Plain ¥700, curry ¥750, pizza ¥750.
Seasoned with soy sauce.
Demi-glace based, so a wheat roux.
Japanese curry is thickened with a wheat-flour roux.

items.en: Napolitan — ketchup spaghetti with sausage and pepper
items.note: The defining Japanese kissaten pasta, invented in postwar Yokohama and nothing to do with Naples: soft-boiled spaghetti fried with ketchup, onion, green pepper and sausage. As a lunch set with salad, soup and drink, ¥1,240.
Lunch set ¥1,230.
Lunch set ¥1,240.

items.ja: ほうれん草とサーモンのクリームパスタ
items.romaji: hourensou to saamon no kuriimu pasuta

items.ja: なすとベーコンのアラビアータ
4種きのこのペペロンチーノ

items.note: Main plus rice, salad, potato salad, soup and a drink — a lot for ¥990. Fixed by day: Monday demi-glace hamburg, Tuesday chicken nanban, Wednesday karaage, Thursday ginger pork, Friday tonkatsu, weekends yakiniku. Every one of those mains is wheat, via panko, batter or soy.
The shop names this as the must-eat: firm and smooth, cut with a spoon rather than wobbling. With a drink, ¥700.

The picture-perfect green soda with a scoop of vanilla — the emblematic Showa kissaten drink. Floats also come as coffee, tea, cola, orange, Calpis, café au lait and cocoa, all ¥610; matcha latte and lemon squash ¥660.
With a drink, ¥1,180. Chocolate and fruit parfaits ¥950.

items.en: Anmitsu — agar jelly cubes with red bean and syrup
items.note: Kanten (agar) cubes, sweet azuki, fruit and black-sugar syrup, sometimes with a scoop of ice cream. With a drink ¥800.
With a drink ¥970.
With a drink ¥850. Sweet-potato pie the same price.
American and iced coffee also ¥460; café au lait and Vienna coffee ¥560.
The Kansai blended banana-and-fruit shake with milk. Banana juice ¥600.
A patisserie with a small cafe on the Higashimuki arcade; you pick from the chilled case, or from a trolley wheeled round the room. Individual cakes run roughly ¥470–¥550.

Yamato-cha is Nara's own tea, grown in the eastern highlands since the 9th century. Macarons are made from almond flour and egg white with no wheat — but they are baked in a wheat kitchen, so ask if it matters. A chocolate version is ¥240; plain macarons about ¥180.
Almond-meringue shells; wheat-free by recipe but not in a dedicated kitchen.

items.ja: メレンゲ・ラズベリー
items.note: Recommended by regulars. Egg white and sugar only, but baked alongside wheat.
Seasonal.
Set with gelatin on a biscuit base.
Sold in gift boxes; two kinds of baked sweet for ¥550, or three-piece boxes at ¥550.
Caramelised almonds on a shortbread base.
Toast with butter or another spread, salad and a drink. Reported at ¥400 in 2013 and ¥420 in 2016.

items.en: Uji kintoki — matcha shaved ice with red bean
items.note: Matcha syrup over shaved ice with sweet azuki beans underneath; 'Uji' means the matcha, 'kintoki' the beans.

One seating, everyone starts together at 6pm; the whole restaurant eats the same course. Reported ¥25,000, or about ¥27,000–¥28,000 with drinks. The name Nikon (而今) is a Zen term meaning 'this very moment'. Kaiseki is built on bonito-and-kombu dashi and soy, so it is neither gluten-free nor vegan without long advance negotiation.
The set-piece of any kaiseki: a square cedar tray of small bites arranged to state the season. This kitchen dresses it for the calendar — a Setsubun bean-throwing version in February, for instance.

Considered the dish that measures a kaiseki chef, because there is nowhere to hide in a clear dashi. Seen here: Kuwana clam shinjo with wild shiitake and house-made bachiko, and a kue-and-matsutake bowl.
Three kinds is typical here — bonito, Spanish mackerel and squid on one visit.
Nuta is a dressing of white miso, vinegar and mustard. Served with Nara's Kujo spring onion and needle squid, with a lemon jelly to sharpen it.
Shiro-amadai from Yawatahama is the rarest of the tilefish. Salt only.
Cured in the restaurant and here unusually finished in miso then briefly grilled. Miso can be barley.

items.ja: 猪と海老芋の白味噌酒粕鍋
items.romaji: inoshishi to ebiimo no shiromiso sakekasu nabe
items.en: Wild boar and shrimp-taro in white miso and sake lees
items.note: Winter. Sake lees is the pressed residue from brewing — it gives a sweet, faintly alcoholic body to the broth. Ebi-imo is a curved taro grown around Kyoto and Nara.

items.ja: 蟹とタケノコの炊き込みご飯
items.romaji: kani to takenoko no takikomi gohan
items.note: Kaiseki always ends with rice; this kitchen cooks it in a clay pot with the season's ingredient. A matsutake donabe rice appears in autumn. Takikomi rice is cooked in soy and dashi, so not gluten-free.
Repeatedly singled out by diners as the best thing on the table. Cured mackerel pressed onto vinegared rice in a long bar and sliced.

items.ja: ふきのとうのブリュレ
items.note: Fukinotou is the first thing to push through the snow in spring, intensely bitter and fragrant; turning it into a brûlée is the kitchen showing off, and by the accounts it works.

items.ja: フルーツのゼリー寄せ
items.note: Made with Kotoka — Nara's own strawberry variety — plus black soybean, broad bean and Melogold citrus. Ask whether it is agar or gelatin.
Not tofu at all — ground sesame set with kudzu starch into a dense, silky block. A Buddhist temple food adopted into kaiseki; here served with sea urchin, which is not vegetarian.

items.ja: プリンとコーヒーのセット
items.note: Price is from a 2013 visit and should be treated as long out of date. Both the pudding and the coffee were described as slow, quiet and good.
The shop serves no lunch at all — the food menu is sweets, and the hotcakes are the substantial end of it. Wheat batter.

The owner left an office career to open this; he hand-picks defective beans out of every batch, roasts to suit each bean, and brews one cup at a time to order. The blends are half price from your second cup onward — an unusually generous house rule.
The house blend with the Blue Mountain swapped for a Caribbean bean, giving a lighter cup.

items.ja: マンデリン・シナール
items.note: Indonesian; a faint citrus note over a balanced body.
Sweet and fruity like blackcurrant, with some acidity.
Six or more blends plus single origins, sold by weight; popular locally as gifts.
One of very few food items here. Comes with Tabasco. The shop opens at 9am, so this is the breakfast.
The ¥160 is for the cookies; the cocoa can be iced.

items.ja: コーヒーアイスゼリー
items.en: Coffee jelly with vanilla ice cream
items.note: Bitter coffee jelly, vanilla ice cream and chocolate chips for crunch. Usually set with gelatin.

The shop's whole premise: vegetables puréed into the dough rather than laid on top, so the loaf itself comes out green or orange. Komatsuna (mustard spinach) and carrot versions are standard, and there is a spinach one. Still wheat bread — the vegetables change the colour and the sweetness, not the gluten. The bakery is run as a supported-employment workshop by the Ms-Net non-profit.
Sliced orange right through. Also made with spinach.
¥310–¥360. Add ¥300–¥350 for a mini salad and a drink. Fillings seen: steamed chicken with kinpira burdock, greens and egg, potato salad, carrot and Spam, keema curry.

items.ja: まるパンサンド（3個セット）
items.note: The shop's own announcement: three of the popular vegetable rolls with different fillings — salmon and onion, fluffy egg, burdock salad in one set; salmon, anko-butter and burdock in the other.
Panko-crumbed patty; the sauce is wheat-based too.
The shop's own note says roughly ¥500–¥610 depending on what goes in: a sandwich or roll-sandwich plus sides and a cake. Contents change daily and you choose the box at the counter.

Named by the shop as its most popular rice dish: rice under a soft omelette with the house hayashi sauce poured over. Comes with a mini salad. Add ¥200–¥250 for a drink set including coffee, tea, Nara cider, minestrone or juice. Hayashi sauce is a wheat roux.
¥1,000 with a ¥200 coffee.

items.ja: ごはんランチ「キーマカレー」
items.note: Balanced meat and vegetable; served with a vegetable-noodle carrot salad. Japanese curry base is a wheat roux.

items.ja: ミニサラダ（にんじんと玉ネギのマリネ）
items.romaji: mini sarada — ninjin to tamanegi no marine
items.en: Mini salad: carrot and onion marinade
items.note: One of three that are out every Tuesday to Friday. Sweet vegetables against a gentle vinegar.

items.ja: オリジナルポテトサラダ
items.note: Chunky and rich. Japanese mayonnaise contains egg.

items.ja: ひじきとキャベツのサラダ
items.note: With the shop's own dressing.
Vegetable-heavy but contains pork.

items.ja: トマトの煮込みハンバーグバーガー

items.note: A seasonal announcement from the shop.
Valentine's only, sold as a two-piece set: chocolate with milk-chocolate chips and strawberry with white-chocolate chips.
Run occasionally rather than daily — check before going.

items.en: Set A — welcome drink, coffee roasted to your taste, and a sweets plate
items.note: The cafe is reservation-only, one party of up to four per slot, ninety minutes, booked by the previous noon. The coffee is roasted for you after you order — say what you like and they roast to it — and refills are included. Note the shop's site has been flagged 'under maintenance' since February 2026, so confirm before travelling.

items.en: Set B — coffee roasted to your taste with a raw cake
items.note: Same coffee, one raw cake instead of the full plate. Refills included.

This is the reason to come and the reason to ask questions. The shop's own description of raw sweets: no egg, no dairy, no wheat flour and no white sugar, nothing heated above 48°C, built from fresh and dried fruit and soaked nuts. That makes them plausibly wheat-free and often dairy-free — but the shop makes no allergen declaration and shares a small kitchen, and some raw recipes use honey. Ask about the specific cake.

items.ja: ローチーズケーキタルト
items.note: 'Cheese' here means blended soaked cashews, not dairy; the base is nuts and dates rather than biscuit. From the shop's own teaching syllabus.
Cacao worked without roasting. A white-chocolate version is made too.
Dates, nuts and cacao pressed rather than baked.
Dried fruit and nuts rolled into bite-size balls.
Green beans from around the world, hand-roasted; the shop also teaches hand-roasting classes. Refills come with both sets.
A raw-food take on the Sichuan noodle — vegetable 'noodles' with a nut-and-sesame sauce, nothing cooked. Lunch is not always available; ask when booking.

items.ja: ローツナマヨ海苔巻き
items.note: The tuna and the mayonnaise are both plant-based reconstructions.
A jun-kissa built around a serious hi-fi system that dominates the middle of the room. Coffee is served by origin.
Reported ¥550–¥650; the shop sometimes knocks ¥50 off as the day's special.
The house everyday cup.
Recommended by regulars alongside a charcoal-roasted option.
Roasting over binchotan charcoal rather than gas gives a rounder, smokier cup.
Reviewers note the shop imports the real thing rather than a domestic blend.
Reported ¥400 in 2017 and ¥500 more recently. Gelatin-set on a biscuit base.
Price is from 2016. Thick-cut and simple — the whole food menu here is essentially toast.

The thing to eat here, and the farm says so itself. Made from that morning's milk, on the oldest working dairy farm in Nara prefecture, right beside Hannya-ji temple. Sold only at the farm shop — the restaurant does not serve it. The shop closes for winter, early December to mid-March.

Low-temperature pasteurised — 75°C for fifteen minutes, the old way — and 100% raw milk with nothing added. The farm still delivers 700–800 bottles a day to houses nearby, and supplies the Nara Hotel. The taste genuinely varies day to day because the cows are fed whatever vegetables the neighbouring farms send over.
Same glass bottle, same recipe as when the farm opened in the Meiji era.

items.ja: 植村牧場特製 牛乳もなか
items.note: Milk ice cream between crisp wafers. The round version has been discontinued. Monaka wafers are usually mochi rice — ask.

The standard: soup (a chilled pumpkin soup on one visit), salad, bread (baguette and a fig loaf) and a main such as hamburg steak in tomato sauce. The chef trained at the Nara Hotel. Bread and demi-glace both mean wheat.
The Ichizu lunch plus a drink and dessert — and the drink can be the farm's own fresh milk. A three-meat version has been served.
Mixed fried items with rice; reported ¥1,300–¥1,400. Panko is wheat.
The cheapest way in.

items.ja: 海老クリームコロッケ
items.note: Thin crumb around a milk-heavy béchamel that runs when you cut it — the farm's own milk is the point. Flour roux plus panko.
Chicken rice wrapped in a barely-set omelette; a long-running favourite here.
Slow-cooked beef in a curry lightened with the farm's milk, giving it a yoghurt-like tang. Japanese curry roux is wheat.
Winter only, made with the farm's milk. A doria version also exists.
Fillet pork with pork-and-miso soup and pickles.

items.ja: いちづ特製アップルパイ（ホール）
items.note: A whole pie packed with apple, sold to take away. The farm suggests warming it in a toaster oven.

items.ja: スイーツセット（珈琲付）
items.note: The cafe menu runs from 2pm.
Can be taken instead of the post-meal coffee in a set.

The entry lunch, tax included. Twelve seats, counter and private rooms, one Michelin star. The menu changes month by month with the market. Kaiseki is built on soy and dashi, so gluten and fish are unavoidable without a long conversation in advance.
Service charge additional.
The same course as dinner, at lunch. Service charge additional. Three lunch courses are offered in total.
A single dinner course, tax included, service charge additional.

items.en: The dashi — southern Hokkaido ma-kombu and aged katsuobushi
items.note: The restaurant names this as the foundation of everything it serves: a generous quantity of premium ma-kombu for depth, with hon-karebushi — bonito dried, smoked and mould-cured over months — from which the dark bloodline has been trimmed away so the stock stays clean. Bonito means no kaiseki course here can be made vegan.

Nara prefecture formally designates a list of traditional local vegetables as Yamato-yasai — among them Yamato-mana greens, the round Yamato-marunasu aubergine, Katahira akane radish and Uda-kin burdock. The kitchen builds seasonal dishes around whatever is in.

Kaiseki was originally food designed to be drunk with, and the restaurant states plainly that each dish is built to complement the sake rather than the other way round. You can choose your own ochoko cup.

items.ja: 焼酎・シャンパン・ワイン・ウイスキー
items.note: Whisky is barley; wine is often animal-fined. You may pick your own glass.

The house loaf, and the price has held remarkably steady — ¥250 for a slab, about ¥310 a full kin. Note there is an unrelated shop in Naramachi also called Kohaku (七福食堂／喫茶古白) — this one is the bakery near Ichijo High School north of Shin-Omiya.
The custard is injected at the till after you pay, and the shop tells you to eat it immediately — the shell is still crisp and the custard still cool for about two minutes.
The standard version of the above, also filled to order.
Also sold as a tea-and-lemon cream bun at ¥160 + tax.

The bagels are the shop's obsession — dense, tightly packed and heavily filled. Filled versions include shiso, roast ham and mozzarella; perilla with cheese; cheese dakgalbi; and Chinese chive with ham.
Made with Omi beef, one of Japan's three great wagyu. Medium heat. A curry frankfurter version is ¥292 including tax; a plain curry pan ¥190.

items.ja: さとうきびのでにっしゅ
items.note: Made with unrefined cane sugar.
Black soybeans from Uda, the highland district east of Nara city.

items.ja: 小豆入あんことれんにゅう
items.note: Whole azuki beans left in the paste.

items.ja: パレード！カンパーニュ
items.note: The shop runs many campagne variants: fig and walnut; cranberry, orange and cream cheese; tea, raisin and cream cheese; blueberry and cream cheese.

items.ja: ワイルドブルーベリーと紅茶 アーモンドとクリームチーズ
items.romaji: wairudo buruuberii to koucha aamondo to kuriimu chiizu
items.en: Wild blueberry, tea, almond and cream cheese

items.note: Snipped and splayed so the loaf comes out shaped like an ear of wheat; you tear the pieces off. Repeatedly named the shop's best item.

items.ja: スモークサーモンの野菜たっぷりサンド
items.romaji: sumooku saamon no yasai tappuri sando
items.en: Smoked salmon sandwich with a lot of vegetables
items.note: Price is from a 2013 report.

items.ja: サーモンとチーズフォンデュデニッシュ
アボカドとソーセージのタコスミート
items.romaji: abokado to sooseeji no takosu miito

items.ja: いちごとクリームチーズのマフィン
items.romaji: ichigo to kuriimu chiizu no mafin
items.note: Price before tax.
Autumn. A candied-chestnut cream version also appears.
Price from an old listing and long out of date; a petit-france is also sold.

The whole reason to come, and it changes every month — there is no fixed dish to order. Vegetables come mainly from the Yazaki farm in Ikoma, the noodle broth and the miso are made in-house, and the cooking follows shokuyojo, the idea of eating to keep the body in balance. One April set was fuki-butterbur mixed sushi, new onion and chicken with crisp bonito flakes, mugwort-fu dengaku, new-potato miso soup and pickles; a summer one was pork yanagawa-style with a soft-cooked egg, mozuku vinegar, colourful namul, nori tsukudani, rice, a lotus-seed soup and syrup-preserved winter melon. Soy, dashi and miso run through everything.
A larger seasonal variant of the monthly set.
The lighter option if you do not want the full teishoku.
For when you want a drink rather than a meal.

Changes every two months and is deliberately small — sized so you can still eat it after the set meal — with real spice and herb aromatics and restrained sweetness. Reported at ¥1,000–¥1,300 depending on the build. Recorded versions: chestnut and rum raisin (white chestnut cream, vanilla ice, granola, rum-raisin ice, dark coffee jelly); hojicha and citrus; Earl Grey and baked apple; caramel nuts and baked apple; strawberry-mascarpone mille-feuille. Granola and mille-feuille both mean wheat.

The owner's own blend, and heavier on spice than most: cinnamon, kola nut, vanilla, clove, lemongrass and cardamom, each roasted first to bring the aroma up. Sold as a glass, or as a ¥1,000 bottle of syrup to take home.

items.ja: 自家製ソーダ（しそ・梅・ジンジャー・レモン）
items.en: House sodas — shiso, plum, ginger, lemon
items.note: Made from house syrups; you can float ice cream on top to make it a soda float.

Brewed through a cloth filter rather than paper, which lets more of the oils through and gives a rounder cup. This was the coffee programme of the neighbouring inn Kohaku, moved into the shokudo; the cafe side still trades under the name Kissa Kohaku.

items.ja: 国産和牛のすき焼き（宿泊者向け）
items.en: Domestic wagyu sukiyaki (for guests at the inn)
items.note: Not served in the shokudo — this is at Kohaku, the owner's guesthouse a minute north, added to the room rate, minimum two people, book ahead. It revives the tradition of Hiyoshikan, the old Nara inn where art and history students gathered and sukiyaki was the house dish. Sukiyaki's warishita sauce is soy, sugar and mirin.

items.ja: 自家製スモーク盛合せ
items.note: The dish to start with. Four kinds: house prosciutto of Baak pork, smoked Piyotama egg, smoked oyster and smoked scallop. Price is per person. Note there is no paper menu here — you read it on a screen but order out loud.

items.ja: ホタルイカと菜の花の和ヒージョ
items.note: The shop's pun: ajillo made Japanese ('wa'). Firefly squid are the tiny bioluminescent squid caught in Toyama Bay in spring; available February to May only.

items.ja: ヤングコーンのカダイフ風フリット
items.en: Baby corn fried in its own silk, kadaif-style
items.note: The corn silk is wound around the cob and fried so it crisps like kadaif pastry — a neat trick. Served with a white-miso aioli. Batter is wheat and aioli contains egg.

items.ja: 鰻肝の赤ワイン煮、香草パン粉仕上げ
items.romaji: unagi-kimo no aka-wain ni, kousou panko shiage
items.en: Eel liver in red wine under herb crumb
items.note: The escargot-in-herb-butter technique applied to eel liver — the clearest statement of what this kitchen does, French method on Japanese ingredients. Panko is wheat.

Chicken-and-beef bouillon set as a jelly, house umeboshi paste, and — the local touch — hand-stretched noodles from Miwa Yamamoto. Miwa in Nara is the birthplace of somen, hand-stretched wheat noodle, made there since at least the 8th century. Topped with Baak pork prosciutto.

items.ja: ヤマトポークの洋風ルーロー天津飯
items.romaji: Yamato Pooku no youfuu ruuroo tenshinhan
items.en: Yamato Pork lu rou fan under a crab-style omelette
items.note: Taiwanese braised pork given French spicing, then capped with egg the way a tenshin-han is. Yamato Pork is Nara's branded pig. Soy sauce throughout.

items.ja: 大和牛の挽き肉カレー
items.note: Took second place in the 2010 black-rice curry competition. Two grinds of beef are used — one fine to build the sauce, one coarse for texture — against vegetable sweetness and tomato acidity. From the shop's earlier premises; ask whether curry is still served. Japanese curry base is a wheat roux.

items.ja: 大和肉鶏手羽先の薬膳カレー
items.en: Medicinal curry with Yamato chicken wings
items.note: Yamato-nikudori is Nara's slow-grown branded chicken, firmer and more flavourful than commodity birds. Yakuzen means the spicing follows Chinese medicinal principles.

items.ja: 季節野菜のベジタリアンカレー
items.note: Explicitly vegetarian on the shop's own listing, which is rare here — but confirm the stock and whether the roux contains dairy. From the earlier premises.
Local sake lengthened with soda; the sake changes daily — Mimurosugi junmai ginjo karakuchi on one visit.
From Toyosawa Brewery in Nara city.

items.ja: 奈良の地酒（純米・純米吟醸・純米大吟醸・燗酒）
items.note: A deep Nara list at roughly ¥700–¥800 a glass — including Harushika from Imanishi Seibei in Nara city, and its 'Nara no Yaezakura', brewed with yeast isolated from cherry petals in a collaboration with Nara Women's University. Nara-grown Hinohikari table rice is used in some of them.
Brewed in Koryo, Nara prefecture. Beer is barley.
There is a ¥500 per-person seat charge — worth knowing before the bill arrives.

Weekdays to 1pm. Caesar-dressed risotto-style leaf salad, your pick of seven spaghetti or two risottos, a small house gelato and a drink. Recent reports put the walk-in lunch nearer ¥1,000–¥1,500. Note the shop is a pasta specialist — it says plainly that it serves nothing but pasta unless you pre-order.

Weekdays 11:30–12:30 only, last order 12:30, and it sells out — after that you go on to the ordinary pasta lunch. Worth phoning or messaging ahead; they take same-day bookings until noon and there is a ¥1,100 no-show charge.

items.ja: 生パスタ（タリアテッレ／リングイネ／パッパルデッレ）
items.en: Fresh pasta — tagliatelle, linguine or pappardelle
items.note: The shop's obsession, and you choose the shape: tagliatelle is an egg noodle cut flat like kishimen, linguine is pressed oval and springy with a faint sweetness, pappardelle is wide and soft. Upgrading a dish to fresh pasta costs about ¥100. Fresh egg pasta means wheat and egg.

items.ja: ガーリックと鷹の爪のピリ辛オイルソース
items.romaji: gaarikku to takanotsume no pirikara oiru soosu
items.en: Garlic and chilli oil spaghetti (aglio e olio)
items.note: The simplest on the list. A tomato version is the same price.

items.ja: 自家製トマトソースとモッツァレラチーズ
items.romaji: jikasei tomato soosu to mottsarera chiizu
items.note: The shop names the fresh tomato and mozzarella pairing as its own favourite.

items.ja: ベーコンときのこのクリームソース
items.romaji: beekon to kinoko no kuriimu soosu
items.note: The same pairing is offered in tomato, tomato-cream and bonito-dashi soy versions, all ¥1,320.

items.ja: ベーコンときのこの鰹だし醤油
items.romaji: beekon to kinoko no katsuo-dashi shouyu
items.en: Bacon and mushroom in bonito-dashi soy
items.note: The wafu (Japanese-style) pasta that Japan invented and Italy never asked for — bonito stock and soy instead of a Mediterranean sauce, and lighter than most cream pastas. Soy sauce is wheat.

items.ja: ベビーホタテのクリームソース
items.note: Also in tomato and tomato-cream at ¥1,320, and with mushroom in dashi-soy at ¥1,300.

items.ja: 黒オリーブとアンチョビのトマトソース
items.romaji: kuro oriibu to anchobi no tomato soosu

items.ja: 自家製スモークチキンのクリームソース
items.romaji: jikasei sumooku chikin no kuriimu soosu
items.note: A spicy tomato version is the same price. The smoking is done in-house.

items.ja: 自家製スモークサーモンのクリームソース
items.romaji: jikasei sumooku saamon no kuriimu soosu
items.note: Cherry-smoked in-house; also appears in the summer course.

items.ja: 海老のトマトクリームソース
items.note: A prawn-and-scallop tomato is the same price.
Add ¥100 to have it on fresh pasta. Pesto contains cheese.
The shop calls it its number-one pizza; house tomato sauce and cheese. Allow about 20 minutes. Note the current site says pizza must be arranged the day before.

items.ja: チーズとブラックペッパー（20cm）
items.en: Cheese and black pepper pizza, no tomato
items.note: Described by the shop as snack-like.

items.ja: 黒オリーブ・ケッパー・アンチョビ（20cm）
items.en: Black olive, caper and anchovy pizza
Meat dish for two or three
items.note: From ¥1,800. Must be arranged by the day before — the shop is a pasta specialist and does not keep these on hand.

items.en: Fish dish for two or three
items.note: From ¥1,700, day-before order.

Order two days ahead. The July–August 2026 run: prosciutto and tomato marinated salad; fresh pasta with prawn and olive tomato; cherry-smoked salmon in basil cream; wagyu tagliata with marsala and balsamic and potato gnocchi; house gelato and cheesecake; coffee or tea. ¥3,200 before tax.
Made in the restaurant; a small scoop comes with the lunch set. Strawberry has been on.

items.ja: きたまちチーズケーキ
items.note: Named for the Kitamachi district the restaurant sits in; a regulars' favourite.
The house signature. Dorayaki is two small pancakes around sweet red bean; here they are cooked only after you order, so it arrives hot rather than wrapped. Wheat batter and egg.

Rice-flour dumplings grilled on a skewer and glazed with a sweet soy syrup — also made to order, so they come off the grill hot. The dumplings themselves are rice, but the mitarashi glaze is soy sauce, which is wheat.

items.ja: 大和茶の抹茶・煎茶・ほうじ茶
items.en: Yamato tea — matcha, sencha and hojicha
items.note: The point of the shop, which opened in spring 2026 as the group's first tea-led room: Nara-grown Yamato-cha, from the highlands east of the city where tea has been cultivated since the 9th century. Served in Akahada-yaki, the local Nara pottery, painted with Nara motifs.

From ¥600. The parent company is a specialty roaster that also wholesales green beans; the water is spring water from the Yoshino district. Hot coffee and lattes come in Akahada-yaki bowls, hot tea in French cups. You smell the options and pick.
Chosen by sniffing the leaf before you commit — the shop hands you the aromas to taste-test.
Spring only. Cherry syrup with a salt-preserved cherry blossom opening on the surface as it warms. Contains dairy.

From ¥300. The group's own loaf, made with Nara-grown wheat and organically farmed ingredients, and named after Mount Mikasa behind Kasuga Shrine. It was created deliberately against the sweet 'luxury shokupan' fashion — hard-looking crust, soft chewy crumb, no sweetness. Wheat.

From ¥2,500. Built on Yamato-yasai heirloom vegetables, Yamato beef, Yamato pork and Yamato chicken from local farms and roadside producers. The group's sandwiches, sausages and hams are supplied to a well-known hotel restaurant.
A proper non-alcoholic list, which is unusual in Nara.
Opening hours are extended on Friday and Saturday evenings for wine. Wine is often animal-fined.

items.en: Kama-nuki udon — noodles straight from the pot
items.note: This is what the shop is for, and it is worth understanding. Normally boiled udon is rinsed in cold water to firm the surface and wash off starch. Kama-nuki skips that: the noodles are lifted straight out of the cauldron and served, so the surface stays soft, starchy and fragrant and the chew is looser than you expect. The dough is hand-kneaded and every strand hand-cut at a board facing the street. Udon is wheat, entirely — nothing here is gluten-free.

items.en: Kake udon — noodles in hot broth
items.note: The plain bowl and the honest test of the noodle. Hot dashi broth over the noodles, nothing else. The broth is bonito-and-kombu dashi with soy, so neither vegan nor gluten-free.
Beef simmered in a sweet-salty soy braise, laid over the noodles. Wagyu options are on the menu, which is unusual at this price bracket.
The shop's headline bowl: beef braised to order in a sweet-salty sauce, tangled with a runny onsen egg so the yolk coats the noodles. Also served cold.
Sesame and chilli in the Sichuan manner, on udon rather than Chinese noodles.

items.en: Kitsune udon — with sweet fried tofu
items.note: A sheet of aburaage simmered in sugar and soy until it is sweet and dripping. Named after the fox, said to love fried tofu — and this is the Kansai form of the dish, where kitsune always means udon.

items.ja: ハイカラうどん（天かす）
items.note: Not a menu line so much as a move: tenkasu, the crisp scraps of fried tempura batter, sit on the counter for you to add yourself, and a bowl of kake plus tenkasu is what Kansai calls haikara udon. The crumbs soften into the broth and enrich it.
Fried to order, not held. One plate held prawn, shishito pepper, aubergine and chicken. Eaten with the table salt or the dashi-soy on the counter rather than dipped in the udon broth.
Tempura is also sold piece by piece — prawn, chicken and aubergine among them.
Chicken in tempura batter rather than karaage dredge — softer, lighter.
Wheat batter and a shared fryer.
Curry broth thickened with starch so it clings to the noodles. Listed in the shop's category tags; ask whether it is on that day.
